reviewMethod: Read-only installed implementation, governing schema/contract and actual regression inspection; independent source-digest audit of parent-executed Rust evidence. No independent Rust test run or code-refinement proof claimed.

reviewObservations.observation: Declaration/source correspondence is required first. SHA256 is computed over retained contract bytes before parsing, then complete structural equality to the corresponding declaration is required. Batch version/hash/rows and each cell member set are closed.

Rows match actual ordered column count; each outcome ID is resolved within its own column and exact disposition must match. Values use the selected original model domain and exact normalization; constant values must equal that declared outcome class.

Parent-executed controls accept equivalent exact large-integer tokens; refuse a different domain-valid value for the selected transform and integer-width overflow. Transformed(null) accepts only the declared nullable domain/value; replacement0 refuses. A later Withheld cell carrying any value refuses the whole batch.

Every cell literal/normalized budget error maps to WFT-LIMIT in result phase. Initial declaration errors remain unchanged. Actual same-domain1M string batches with2 or6cells pass;8cells below the32MiB parser limit refuse WFT-LIMIT, isolating aggregate cell ledger exhaustion.

Method returns Result<()> only after all cells pass and emits no partial object, release token or callback. Empty rows still require declaration/source/hash agreement and do not imply query permission.

No policy-truth or outcome-selection correspondence is established. Scalar result domains/Absent stay outside initial direct declaration subset; native codecs, current authority, installation and guarded release remain open. Compiler lowering remains unconditionally refused.

scope: Pure owner-context contract/cell correspondence for the selected direct-field model-domain subset. This review does not establish runtime policy truth, authorized outcome selection, native value/source correspondence, streaming release, compiler lowering or backend acceptance.
